formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question.

formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question.

open_details: Legal transport history for delayed same-ballot AcceptSync.
core_gaps: Complete initialization, storage reconstruction and read classification path; inspect runtime caller/delivery responsibilities before declaring the combined backbone usable.
before.rationale: Initial sourced backbone with explicit incomplete support boundaries; no violation or execution result is claimed.

formation.explanation: Append is buffered during prepare, sent locally during Leader/Accept, or forwarded. Current-ballot promises populate participant slots; a prepare quorum selects maximal accepted-round/index history, synchronizes it, then sends AcceptSync. Followers synchronize and acknowledge, and incremental appends use sequence validation. Current-ballot Accepted messages update leader indexes; a write quorum causes decided-index advancement and decision propagation. Read APIs expose the decided prefix for application use. Storage load reconstructs accepted extent and reads classify entries against the decided boundary. The optional actor tracks a client EntryId to an assigned end index and ballot; on ticks it resolves success using decided index before testing ballot supersession.

context.explanation: Tick drives BLE; matching heartbeat rounds/configurations influence leader selection. SequencePaxos requires a higher ballot before initiating preparation. Followers persist a higher promise, reject lower-ballot replication and accept same-ballot prepare only during recovery. Reconnect and sequence gaps can initiate equal-ballot recovery. StopSign seals the old log and delegates startup/state transfer of a new configuration to the caller. Construction reads the stored promise into protocol and BLE recovery context, while cached accepted metadata comes from the backend. The actor serializes incoming messages and commands but runs completion processing only on tick branches.

connection.explanation: Authority alone does not enable acceptance: the new leader first gathers promise support and adopts accepted history, including prior decisions, before appending buffered work. A stopped selected history blocks appends. Followers require the promised ballot and appropriate phase; incremental old-session work is rejected or triggers recovery. Equal-ballot recovery resets phase and sequence before synchronization, leaving a specific delayed-AcceptSync history question. Client assignment records survive incoming higher-ballot synchronization until a later notifier drain. Whether the assigned entry survives depends on adopted history, rather than on numeric decided-index advancement alone.

before.meaning: Replica has recorded the ballot to which its acceptance handling is currently promised.
before.validity_context: Stored promise ballot; equal-ballot recovery can change phase and session without increasing it.
before.durability: Written through storage; actual storage failure and recovery semantics not yet fully traced.
before.recovery: Constructor seeing a stored promise starts Recover and queues PrepareReq; precise backend reconstruction remains open.
unknowns: Storage backend persistence and atomicity contracts.

after.meaning: Replica has recorded the ballot to which its acceptance handling is currently promised.
after.validity_context: Stored promise ballot; equal-ballot recovery can change phase and session without increasing it.
after.durability: Promise is stored through Storage and loaded at construction. MemoryStorage is volatile; PersistentStorage stores it in RocksDB. Crash durability of backend settings remains a separate unknown.
after.recovery: InternalStorage::load_cache reads the backend promise; SequencePaxos constructor enters Recover when get_promise returns Some and sends PrepareReq. BLE initializes from recovered promise with its own recovery round.
unknowns: Persistent backend crash durability under configured options.

after.meaning: Pending client operation has a recorded assigned log end index and assignment ballot, associated by its EntryId.
after.validity_context: Recorded assignment under its supplied ballot; this record alone does not establish that the same entry remains at the index after later synchronization.
after.durability: Volatile actor state; removed on completion/error and lost at actor shutdown.
after.recovery: No reconstruction of Pending records on actor restart is implemented in ActorState::new.
unknowns: Preservation of operation-to-entry association across a higher-ballot synchronization before completion.

after.reason: Does numeric decided-index success precede recognition that a different entry replaced this pending operation under a new ballot?

before.system_boundary: Captured OmniPaxos core, storage and runtime; caller owns network delivery and application consumption. In-repository runtime and storage backends are not yet mapped.

after.system_boundary: Captured OmniPaxos core, storage and optional async runtime. Caller owns message transport and application consumption; actor owns ticking, command serialization and append-notification completion.
